notes:
From repair-shop (from: repair-shop), refitted Tue Oct 27 and merged on the REDESIGN 2 master (frozen 9:17am). A sharpening shop runs like a repair shop's quick side: the knives are dropped off, an edge check is OK'd only for damaged blades, a written estimate is OK'd before any work, and READY comes before the pick-up. No base plug-in or old flowchart existed (new profession); the plug-in is built from the trade's norm.
Two companies: Lee's Sharpening (the master's barbershop, flow A: the shop for knives, shears and tools) and Lee Mobile Sharpening (the master's Lee Home Services, flow B: a truck that sharpens at homes, kitchens and salons). Kinds of work: plumbing became knife sharpening, electrical became salon shear service, the later NEW kind is saw sharpening (B) and scissor sharpening (A). People: Riley and Avery became Gus and Rita (the shop); Jordan and Casey became Hank and Nora (the truck), so the master's pronouns still fit (Jordan he, Casey she). Addresses: 205 Foundry St (the shop), 4 Maple Ct (Alex), 310 Grove Ave (the second site).
No license: sharpening needs no person license; the business gives its registration where the city or state asks (S1-60 '1 A license', S2-28 '1 Yes, each one' and S11-42's two license branches are off; the sign-up license sentences are reworded as registration only).
Flow A money: main list|none|counter (a $35 knife set, up to 5 knives, from the board: nothing taken, paid at the counter), visit|none|counter (a rusty or chipped set priced after a look: the $10 edge check is promised, Gus's written estimate is $110 blade restoration + $15 edge polish = $125 with the check included), list|none|bill (the bill goes with READY). The shop saves no card, holds nothing, takes no deposit and no full price: no cancel or no-show fee at the shop.
Flow B money: main list|card|card ($179 kitchen visit, up to 30 knives and tools, at the customer's place; a card is saved for the $89 trip fee, which is the late-cancel and no-show fee, charged only on Sam's yes, and owed after a no to a visit price: B4-14; the sharpener works alone, so the saved card is charged for the visit at DONE), list|card|bill (Rosie texts the bill), visit|card|bill (a big mixed batch priced at the visit), list|none|bill (a restaurant kitchen on account: nothing taken, the bill after). No deposit and no full price anywhere. All amounts have names per path.
Facts: dropoff (knives left at the shop), extrawork (a chip or crack found at the bench, OK'd first). No photos fact: sharpening is priced from the board or after a look. No documents fact: the written estimate is the visit path's own price OK, so B8-93's 'An estimate becomes its own job' branch is off. No switches. Settings: A a set start (drop-off slots), B a 2-hour window; cutoff A 7am the day of, B 6pm the day before (the truck's route is planned the evening before).
Safety: fire, sparks near fuel or a bad cut stops the booking; a cracked or loose blade, a chipped blade that could break, or a bare blade carried loose gets the safety steps, then the booking goes on, marked urgent. A crack found during sharpening stops the work (B8-30). A child never books or drops off blades (A4-24 / B4-32 'A child' off).
Own step: A8-x01, the count and tag at the counter (every piece counted with the customer and listed on the ticket, checked again at pick-up), a real first step of this trade.
Offs for work this shop never has: video or phone (A4-01, B4-01), plans and insurance, packages, a person by name, plan steps, rented items, 'too few booked', a child left, stage billing, next visit at checkout, a signed contract, nobody-home branches and sent-now steps.
Not sure (for the verifier): S1-13's sign-up example card still lists 'Paid in full' lines and a $20 fee for services this shop never prepays (master text); A8-02 keeps the 'something required is missing' branch for loose, unwrapped blades; a restaurant on a standing route would be a repeat plan, which this build leaves to the master's plan branches (off in flow A, offered in B only as the master's example); the $179 kitchen visit is the master's number, kept so sums and fees stay right.
